guide.text: Tap the two-beat march. Compare the dotted opening figure with the short chords and rests that answer it.
The opening gesture returns, then climbs higher. Follow the C-sharp leading into the D-major ending of the phrase.
Compare these phrases with bars 1–8. Keep the short notes clear and the marching pulse steady.
Both hands begin with the same rhythm an octave apart. Listen to how the chordal answers contrast with that shared line; this section repeats through the ending.
Recognize the opening phrase again. Compare its familiar G-major sound with the contrasting passage.
The hands move together again before the final G-major chord. Observe the written rests and the repeat back to bar 17.

score.title: The Wild Rider (Wilder Reiter), Op. 68 No. 8
score.subtitle: Robert Schumann · solo piano · complete

guide.text: The E pickup launches a quick six-eighth-note pattern. Hear the A-minor melody above the short accompaniment chords; G-sharp pulls back toward A.
The opening phrase returns and closes on A. The repeat includes the opening pickup; the remaining short part of bar 8 introduces the next section.
The tune moves to the left hand in an F-major setting while the right hand plays the chords. Isolate the lower staff to hear the melodic role change.
Compare this lower-hand statement with bars 9–12. The right-hand E at the end of bar 16 prepares the return.
The melody returns to the right hand in A minor. Compare the hand roles with the middle section.
Recognize the closing phrase and its G-sharp–A arrival. Keep the final rests as precise as the moving notes.

score.title: The Happy Farmer (Fröhlicher Landmann), Op. 68 No. 10
score.subtitle: Robert Schumann · solo piano · complete

guide.text: The left-hand C pickup leads into the main tune. Listen below the right-hand offbeat chords: the lower staff carries the melody.
The opening tune returns. Compare the left-hand line with the right-hand chords, then hear the upper C that launches the next phrase.
The right hand sings a longer line while inner notes continue the accompaniment. Separate the upper voice from the chord tones underneath it.
Hear the short closing answer and the return to F. The final C pickup prepares another upper-hand phrase.
Compare the returning upper phrase with bars 9–12. Keep its long notes singing while the accompaniment remains light.
The closing gestures settle on F major. Observe the final rest rather than adding an extra chord.

guide.text: The high G pickup leads into a falling line with D-sharp rising to E. Hear the melody alone before the lower sustained notes enter.
The line descends into a lower register. Follow the changing bass and the rising notes that prepare the next high G.
Compare this statement with the opening. The E-minor phrase closes before a new E pickup begins the repeated section at the end of bar 16.
The contrasting phrase moves around C and A, with overlapping held tones. Isolate each hand to follow how the lines fit together.
The opening falling gesture appears among changing inner voices. Listen for the high G that prepares the return.
Recognize the opening melody again and compare its quieter ending with the earlier statements.
The harmony changes beneath the lower melody before the final E-minor chord. Follow the tied bass, then take the written repeat back to the pickup at the end of bar 16.
